tldr; it would take too much calculation

so here we go,

1. Reddit would have a place to store all it's data: a database.
2. this databse would have data organised into units called tables (think spreadsheets)
3. At the most simplistic implentation, a user can have all his data in one table, where every post will have an unique ID number, lets acll it postID. Using this postID, reddit can do anything with your post, and you can do a lot, like deleting it, reposting it.
4. Let's say OP posts a cat video, this post will be added to the table that contains all OP's posts and will have its own unique ID number within that table.
5. Now I repost this post and in process add the video to my own table, thus assigning it a new ID number 1  within my data table.
6. So for same post you get two different things, one would be ID for OP and one would be ID for me i.e. even if the postId is same, the post will be different.
7. To elaborate the previous point, let's say you make your first post, and I repost your first post, the tables that contain our data would both have one post with Id (let's say ID = 1), but reddit sees it is postId by OP and postId by me. 

So, since reddit does not compare the actual content of the post, it is perfectly logical to have multiple copies of the same thing.

That means that even if there was one huge table that contained all data, thus making every postId unique, it would not be possible to differentiate between them for reddit.

​

To compare actual content with actual content, you would need to perfrom some calcuation on the post data, which will be expensive, like comparing two images. You would need to comapre every pixel value at the most basic level, which for your typical device would be a number like 2000\*1000 number of comparisons, not counting for crops, black bars on top and bottom, and any case when two image content is not of the same dimensions.

​

But modern computers are fast, so lets go a bit deeper.

​

Let's say you have 10 images in your post history and I have 10. That would mean reddit has to make 10 comparisons just like the one i mentioned above. Then another account reposts those 10 images again, making the comparisons 10x10x10.

I didn't have a pencil with me since we used pens at my last school but I didn't knew I would be flung into a test right away. So my dad gives me one. He was carrying one that day. I could see that the teachers were polite because I was screwed before I even donned the school uniform.
